title: Airline Notices and the Penalty Carried on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
What an airline notice standing on the booking does to the penalty taken off the value placed on the voucher, under the Air Ticket Fare Brands terms, follows whether the airline cancelled a segment or only moved one, whether or not the move was large enough to give the traveller a right of its own.

**Terms.**

1. Where a notice standing on the booking records that the airline cancelled a segment, no part of the penalty standing on the booking is taken off the value placed on the voucher.
2. Where a notice standing on the booking records a move short of a cancellation, the share taken is 0.5, so half of the penalty standing on the booking is taken off the value placed on the voucher.
3. Where no such notice stands on the booking, the whole of the penalty standing on the booking is taken off the value placed on the voucher.

Where a notice recording that the airline cancelled a segment stands on the booking, no part of the penalty is taken off whatever else stands on it, including a notice of a move short of a cancellation. A move recorded as short of a cancellation is treated alike whether or not it was large enough to give the traveller a right of its own.

**On hypothetical figures.** Take a penalty of 200.00 US dollars standing on a booking. Where a notice of an airline cancellation stands on it, none of that 200.00 US dollars is taken off the value placed on the voucher. Where the only notice standing records a move short of a cancellation, the share taken is 0.5 and 100.00 US dollars is taken off the value placed on the voucher. Where no notice stands, the whole 200.00 US dollars is taken off the value placed on the voucher.
